expectedText:
COOGAN LAW TRUST ACCOUNT (MINOR'S ENTERTAINMENT EARNINGS) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Productions, Inc.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's "Coogan Law" trust-account requirement, Family Code §§ 6750-6753, as it may relate to a contract between Riley Morgan Lee, a minor, and Acme Productions, Inc. for artistic, creative, or other services within the scope of that chapter. It states facts about when that chapter requires a portion of a minor's earnings under such a contract to be set aside in trust, and about the trust account itself. This corpus separately includes a California Talent Agencies Act information sheet, which addresses who may lawfully procure entertainment employment for an artist, and a Minor Work Permits information sheet, which addresses the school-issued work-permit requirement for minors employed generally. Neither of those sheets addresses the trust-account requirement described here, and this sheet does not address theirs. This document does not state whether any particular contract involving Riley Morgan Lee is of a type covered by Family Code §§ 6750-6753, does not calculate the amount required to be set aside under any specific contract, and does not tell Acme Productions, Inc., Riley Morgan Lee, or Morgan Lee what to do about any particular contract, earnings, or trust account.

WHAT CONTRACTS THIS CHAPTER COVERS, AND WHETHER COURT APPROVAL IS REQUIRED TO TRIGGER IT
Family Code Chapter 3 of Part 3 of Division 11 applies to specific categories of contract between an unemancipated minor and a third party entered into on or after January 1, 2000, including a contract under which a minor is employed or agrees to render artistic or creative services (defined to include acting, dancing, music, comedy, singing, stunt work, voice-over work, content creation, and other performing or entertainment roles, among others), a contract disposing of literary, musical, or dramatic properties or of rights in a person's likeness, voice, performance, or life story for entertainment-industry use, and a contract under which a minor is employed or agrees to render services as a sports participant or player.

A separate section of the same chapter, Family Code § 6751, allows a party to petition the superior court to approve such a contract, which then cannot later be disaffirmed on the ground that it was entered into during minority. But court approval of the contract is not what triggers the trust obligation described in this document. Family Code § 6752 imposes the trust requirement in both situations: where a court approves the contract, and, separately, where the contract is not submitted for court approval at all, or where the court denies approval.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This chapter applies to the following types of contracts entered into between an unemancipated minor and a third party on or after January 1, 2000: (1) A contract pursuant to which a minor is employed or agrees to render artistic or creative services, either directly or through a third party, including, but not limited to, a personal services corporation (loan-out company), or through a casting agency."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6750(a), Family Code § 6750(a) (contracts covered by this chapter) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6750.)
  "Notwithstanding any other statute, in an order approving a minor’s contract of a type described in Section 6750, the court shall require that 15 percent of the minor’s gross earnings pursuant to the contract be set aside by the minor’s employer, except an employer of a minor for services as an extra, background performer, or in a similar capacity, as described in paragraph (3) of subdivision (b) of Section 6750."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6752(b)(1), Family Code § 6752(b)(1) (trust required when a court approves the contract) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6752.)
  "for any minor’s contract of a type described in Section 6750 that is not being submitted for approval by the court pursuant to Section 6751, or for which the court has issued a final order denying approval, 15 percent of the minor’s gross earnings pursuant to the contract shall be set aside by the minor’s employer"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6752(c)(1), Family Code § 6752(c)(1) (trust also required when the contract is not submitted for approval, or approval is denied) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6752.)
  Known gap: Family Code §§ 6750-6753 were fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using different User-Agent strings; after stripping the surrounding page markup and normalizing whitespace, the statutory text returned was byte-identical on both fetches for every section quoted in this document. This clause cites Family Code § 6750(a) (the definition of covered contracts) together with § 6752(b)(1) and § 6752(c)(1) (the two circumstances that trigger the set-aside requirement); § 6750 is an independent section from § 6752, but § 6752(b) and § 6752(c) are both subdivisions of the same section and are not independent of one another. This clause does not quote § 6750's full list of covered contract types (including its provisions on loan-out companies, casting agencies, and content creators) or its separate rules for who counts as the minor's "employer" in each scenario; a reader whose situation may involve a loan-out company, casting agency, or online content platform should not assume coverage or non-coverage based on this summary alone. This document does not address Family Code § 6751 beyond noting that court approval exists as an option and is not the trigger for the trust requirement.

THE 15% SET-ASIDE AND THE MEANING OF "GROSS EARNINGS"
For a contract covered by this chapter, Family Code § 6752 sets the required set-aside at 15 percent of the minor's gross earnings under the contract, to be set aside by the minor's employer and held in trust for the minor's benefit — with an express exception for an employer of a minor working as an extra, background performer, or in a similar capacity. Family Code § 6750(d)(1) defines "gross earnings," for purposes of this chapter, as the total compensation payable to the minor under the contract or, where the minor's services are rendered through a third-party individual or loan-out company, the total compensation payable to that third party for the minor's services. A separate, narrower definition applies specifically to a minor employed as a musician, singer, songwriter, musical producer, or arranger, which this document does not restate here.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Notwithstanding any other statute, in an order approving a minor’s contract of a type described in Section 6750, the court shall require that 15 percent of the minor’s gross earnings pursuant to the contract be set aside by the minor’s employer, except an employer of a minor for services as an extra, background performer, or in a similar capacity, as described in paragraph (3) of subdivision (b) of Section 6750."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6752(b)(1), Family Code § 6752(b)(1) (15 percent set-aside requirement) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6752.)
  "For purposes of this chapter, the minor’s “gross earnings” means the total compensation payable to the minor under the contract or, if the minor’s services are being rendered through a third-party individual or personal services corporation (loan-out company), the total compensation payable to that third party for the services of the minor."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6750(d)(1), Family Code § 6750(d)(1) (definition of "gross earnings") (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6750.)
  Known gap: Family Code §§ 6750 and 6752 were fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using different User-Agent strings; the statutory text returned was byte-identical on both fetches after normalizing whitespace. This clause cites Family Code § 6750(d)(1) and § 6752(b)(1), which are independent sections of the same chapter, not subdivisions of one section. It does not restate the alternative "gross earnings" definition in § 6750(d)(2) for musicians, singers, songwriters, musical producers, and arrangers, which excludes deductions to offset advances or other employer expenses; a reader whose situation involves that category of work should not assume the general definition quoted here applies to them. It also does not restate the extra/background-performer carve-out's cross-reference to § 6750(b)(3) in any further detail.

THE COOGAN TRUST ACCOUNT: WHERE IT MUST BE HELD AND WHEN THE MINOR CAN ACCESS IT
Family Code § 6753 requires the trustee to establish the required trust account — which the statute itself names a "Coogan Trust Account" — at a bank, savings and loan institution, credit union, brokerage firm, or company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, located in California (unless a similar trust has already been established), within seven business days after the minor's contract is signed. The account must be held at a financial institution that remains insured by the FDIC, SIPC, or NCUSIF (or their successors), or with a company that remains registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940.

The account is blocked in the sense that, before the beneficiary turns 18 or a declaration of the minor's emancipation issues, no withdrawal may be made by the beneficiary or anyone else without a written order of the superior court. Once the beneficiary turns 18, the funds may be withdrawn only after the beneficiary provides the financial institution with a certified copy of their birth certificate.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The trustee or trustees shall establish a trust account, that shall be known as a Coogan Trust Account, pursuant to this section at a bank, savings and loan institution, credit union, brokerage firm, or company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, that is located in the State of California, unless a similar trust has been previously established"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6753(a), Family Code § 6753(a) (establishing the Coogan Trust Account) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6753.)
  "Except as otherwise provided in this section, prior to the date on which the beneficiary of the trust attains the age of 18 years or the issuance of a declaration of emancipation of the minor under Section 7122, no withdrawal by the beneficiary or any other individual, individuals, entity, or entities may be made of funds on deposit in trust without written order of the superior court"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6753(b), Family Code § 6753(b) (blocked until age 18 or emancipation) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6753.)
  "The trust shall be established in California either with a financial institution that is and remains insured at all times by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC), or the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund (NCUSIF) or their respective successors, or with a company that is and remains registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6753(d), Family Code § 6753(d) (financial institution insurance/registration requirements) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6753.)
  Known gap: Family Code § 6753 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using different User-Agent strings; the statutory text returned was byte-identical on both fetches after normalizing whitespace. This clause quotes subsections (a), (b), and (d) of the same section, § 6753, so these citations are not independent of one another. This document does not restate subsection (c)'s detail on the trustee's written statement, or subsection (e)'s provisions permitting the financial institution to transfer funds or invest them in specified index funds, government securities, or similar instruments; a reader with questions about how funds already in a Coogan Trust Account may be moved or invested should not rely on this summary alone.

WHAT HAPPENS IF NO TRUSTEE'S STATEMENT IS PROVIDED: TRANSFER TO THE ACTORS' FUND OF AMERICA
Family Code § 6752 states a specific consequence when the trust account is not set up and documented in time: if a parent, guardian, or trustee fails to give the minor's employer a true and accurate photocopy of the trustee's statement (the document identifying the account and financial institution, described in § 6753(c)) within 180 days after the minor's employment begins, the employer must forward the 15 percent set-aside, along with identifying information about the minor, to The Actors' Fund of America, which then becomes trustee of those funds. The statute does not describe this outcome as an escheat to the state; instead, it directs the funds to this specific charitable organization, and separately exempts funds received by The Actors' Fund of America under this chapter from the state's Unclaimed Property Law.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If a parent, guardian, or trustee fails to provide the minor’s employer with a true and accurate photocopy of the trustee’s statement pursuant to Section 6753 within 180 days after the commencement of employment, the employer shall forward to The Actors’ Fund of America 15 percent of the minor’s gross earnings pursuant to the contract"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6752(b)(9)(A), Family Code § 6752(b)(9)(A) (forwarding to The Actors' Fund of America after 180 days) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6752.)
  "All funds received by The Actors’ Fund of America pursuant to this section shall be exempt from the application of the Unclaimed Property Law (Title 10 (commencing with Section 1300) of Part 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure), including, but not limited to, Section 1510 of the Code of Civil Procedure."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 6752(h), Family Code § 6752(h) (exemption from the Unclaimed Property Law) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=6752.)
  Known gap: Family Code § 6752 was fetched twice from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov as separate HTTP requests using different User-Agent strings; the statutory text returned was byte-identical on both fetches after normalizing whitespace. This clause cites § 6752(b)(9)(A) and § 6752(h), both subdivisions of the same section, so they are not independent of one another. This document quotes only the 180-day, court-approved-contract version of this consequence in § 6752(b)(9)(A); a materially parallel 180-day rule appears in § 6752(c)(7)(A) for contracts not submitted for court approval, which this document does not separately quote because the two provisions largely track each other. This document does not describe § 6752(e) and (f), governing how The Actors' Fund of America must then manage, account for, and pay interest on funds it holds as trustee, or the further transfer and disbursement mechanics in § 6752(e)(3); a reader whose funds have been forwarded to The Actors' Fund of America should not assume this summary states everything that governs those funds.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND SIGNATURE
Please sign below to indicate receipt and review of this information sheet.

Minor: Riley Morgan Lee
Employer: Acme Productions, Inc.
Parent or legal guardian: Morgan Lee
Proposed trustee of the Coogan Trust Account: Morgan Lee
Date: September 4, 2026

Acme Productions, Inc. certifies that this information sheet was provided to Morgan Lee in connection with a contract involving Riley Morgan Lee.

Company representative: _______________ Date: _______________

Parent or legal guardian: _______________ Date: September 4, 2026

This sheet is an informational record only. It is not a trustee's statement under Family Code § 6753(c), a court order under Family Code §§ 6751 or 6752, or confirmation that a Coogan Trust Account has been established for Riley Morgan Lee. Completing or signing it does not itself establish a trust account, satisfy any set-aside obligation, or waive any requirement of Family Code §§ 6750-6753.
